title: About
text:
I was born in Washington, DC and grew up in Virginia. I earned my bachelor’s degree in biomedical sciences from Old Dominion University, and I’m now a Master of Public Health student at Morehouse School of Medicine (Class of 2027) and an intern with the Center of Excellence on Environmental Health and Sustainability.
My work sits at the meeting point of public health, technology, and the communities that carry the cost of both.

title: About
text:
What I’m working on
My current research develops a Community-Negotiated Public Health Model for Fair Data Center Development and Management. As AI infrastructure expands, data centers are being sited in neighborhoods with little say in the decision and little visibility into the environmental and health consequences. Using JBI scoping review methodology, the PCC framework, and stakeholder mapping, I’m building a portable model that puts community negotiation at the center of how these projects get planned, approved, and managed.
I’m also part of a client project examining how energy choices shape air quality and health outcomes across Atlanta neighborhood planning units.

title: About
text:
What drives me
I’m interested in environmetal sustainbily and emerging technolgies result in social and behvaior health issues. That means asking who the technology serves, who absorbs its externalities, and what it would take to shift that balance. Long term, I want to bring these tools into orthopedic and sports medicine care, and to build a health equity center in my own community.

title: Projects
text:
A client project with Georgia Power under the Health Solutions Advisement Group, examining how energy choices shape air quality and health outcomes across Atlanta’s neighborhood planning units. The work focuses on NPU T and NPU V, tracking asthma as the primary respiratory link alongside diabetes and cancer as secondary burdens, from 2020 to 2026. The framework traces the pathway from historical drivers like redlining and housing disinvestment through present-day energy burden and air quality exposure, and back again through reinvestment and policy.
